glossary_subtitle: Every indicator has one definition, used everywhere: reports, the report builder, exports, the API, Power BI and the daily history.
glossary_modules_note: Indicators that belong to a module switched off for your organisation are not listed.
glossary_no_list: No page lists these people yet.
common_population: Population: active employees within your clearance. Leavers, erased people and cancelled hires are never counted. The sites add up to the total; people without a site form a « No site » row.
common_unmeasured: Not measured: an absence of measurement is never shown as a result (never 0 %, never « 0 of 0 »). An indicator with nothing to divide by says « Not measured yet ».
common_small_n: Small groups: below 5 people no percentage is shown, only the counts (« 2 of 3 »).
common_requirements: Required skills: always the full set of requirements the department defined for the role; nothing is sampled or trimmed.
common_bands: Status: Compliant from {{threshold}} %, Watch from 50 %, At risk below 50 %, unless the indicator has its own rule. {{threshold}} % is the readiness threshold of the settings.
common_freshness: Freshness: « Live » is computed when you open the page; « Daily history » comes from the snapshot taken every day.
common_delta: Change: compared with the snapshot of about a month earlier, and only between snapshots computed with the same definition; absent when there is none, never « +0 ».
common_drill: Detail: each figure is the length of an exact list of people or items; where a page lists them, the definition links to it.
common_modules: Modules: an indicator that belongs to a module switched off is not shown at all; it never appears as « Not measured ».
common_capability: Level reached: a level above the requirement counts as the requirement. Reaching it is « met », and a surplus never makes up for a gap on another skill or another person, so no role, unit or framework figure goes above 100 %. Compared with another role, every skill is re-evaluated against that role’s requirement.
common_fresh_assessed: « Assessments under 12 months » (health score): the share of the ASSESSED requirements whose latest evidence is under 12 months old. Never-assessed requirements count in the coverage (K3) only.
glossary_contract_changed: Version kpi-2 changed definitions (the level credited at most at the requirement, freshness over the assessed requirements, the K14 median): movements and « What changed » restart from the first kpi-2 snapshot, they never compare two versions.
owner_training: Training manager or local HR administrator
owner_hr_director_hse: HR director and health and safety manager
state_no_requirement: No requirement defined for the role
steps_not_tracked: Steps not tracked for this campaign
k14_not_captured: Role start dates are recorded from this version onwards, at each role change and for each joiner; people already in post have none, and no date is ever assumed. Until someone with a recorded start date has reached « Ready », this indicator is not measured.
k1_def: Share of the people with a verdict who meet the requirements of their role.
k1_formula: Ready ÷ (Ready + Not ready). « Ready » = every requirement assessed, readiness at or above the threshold and every critical skill met. « Not ready » = fully assessed and below, or an assessed critical skill not met.
k1_incl: « Partially assessed » and « Not assessed » are shown beside the rate as counts, never inside it. Always printed with « of N assessed · coverage Y % ».
k1_bands: Compliant from the threshold · Watch from 50 · At risk below 50.
k2_def: Mean readiness, in points, of the people with at least one assessed requirement.
k2_formula: Mean of ( Σ min(level reached, level required) ÷ Σ level required ) over each person's assessed requirements.
k2_den: People with at least one assessed requirement.
k2_incl: A requirement never assessed is not a zero: it is left out of the mean and counted in the coverage.
k3_def: Share of the expected evidence that exists.
k3_formula: Σ assessed requirements (person × requirement) ÷ Σ expected requirements (person × requirement).
k3_den: The full set of requirements of the roles of the population.
k3_incl: No requirement is sampled or dropped.
k3_bands: Compliant from the threshold · Watch from 50 · below 50 « Insufficient coverage » (amber, never red).
k4_def: Of the critical requirements already assessed, the share that is met.
k4_formula: Critical requirements met ÷ critical requirements assessed. « Not demonstrated » (never assessed) is a separate count.
k4_incl: Only the « critical » flag of the requirement counts. The percentage is rounded down, so a single shortfall never reads 100 %.
k4_bands: Compliant = 100 · Watch from 95 · At risk below 95.
k5_def: Share of the critical roles with at least one successor ready now.
k5_formula: Critical roles with at least one « Ready » successor for that role ÷ critical roles.
k5_den: Roles with a criticality of 4 or more held by at least one person in scope.
k5_incl: A successor is active, named on a live succession plan and is not the incumbent. « Ready » is the role-ready rule applied to the target role.
k5_bands: Compliant from the threshold · Watch from 50 · At risk below 50.
k6_name: Critical roles without a ready successor
k6_def: Number of critical roles with no successor ready now, with the list of these roles.
k6_formula: Critical roles − critical roles with a ready successor.
k6_incl: As bench strength. No critical role designated: « To be set up », never a green 0.
k6_bands: 0 Compliant · 1 to 2 Watch · 3 or more At risk.
k7_def: Critical skills held at the required level by exactly one active person in a site.
k7_formula: Number of (site × critical skill) pairs with a single holder.
k7_incl: A holder is a person whose role requires the skill, assessed at or above the required level, certificate not lapsed. Holders are counted within your scope only.
k7_bands: 0 Compliant · 1 to 3 Watch · more than 3 At risk.
k8_name: Certifications expired or expiring within 90 days
k8_def: Two counts shown together: the people with a required certification expired, and the people with a required certification expiring within 90 days.
k8_formula: Expired = valid until before today; expiring = valid until between today and today + 90 days (the « within 30 days » figure is a subset).
k8_den: — (counts of people; the number of certificates is also given)
k8_incl: Only the certifications required by the person's role or by a safety rule. Nothing required: « No certification configured », never 0. A required certificate never recorded is counted apart.
k8_bands: Expired: 0 Compliant, 1 or more At risk; nothing expired but a required certificate missing: Watch. Expiring within 90 days: for information.
k9_def: Share of the people on a role with blocking safety requirements who meet all of them today.
k9_formula: People meeting all their blocking requirements ÷ people concerned whose requirements are evidenced. « Not demonstrated » is a separate count. A running waiver is not fitness.
k9_den: People on a role with at least one blocking safety requirement whose requirements are evidenced, met or not; a known shortfall is always counted.
k9_incl: No role concerned: « No safety requirement configured ». Rules in observe mode do not block. The percentage is rounded down.
k9_bands: Compliant = 100 · Watch from 95 · At risk below 95.
k11_def: The funnel of each campaign in progress: invited, started, submitted, validated.
k11_formula: Validated ÷ invited. A campaign is in progress while it is open and its window contains today, or while its reviews are running (locked); several campaigns are shown separately, never added up.
k11_incl: No campaign: « No campaign in progress », never 0 %. Approved assessments that belong to another campaign are counted apart.
k11_bands: Time-aware: validated at least the elapsed share of the window Compliant; more than 20 points behind At risk.
k12_def: Mean gap between the level people give themselves and the validated level.
k12_formula: Mean of (self level − validated level) over the pairs where both exist, and the share of gaps of 2 levels or more.
k12_incl: Only official levels that a reviewer or evidence validated; a level coming from the self-assessment alone is never a validated level.
k12_bands: |mean| up to 0.3 Compliant · up to 0.7 Watch · above 0.7 At risk.
k13_def: Did development actions move the skill they targeted?
k13_formula: People whose targeted skill rose by at least one credited validated level ÷ people who completed such an action. Actions: completed development-plan actions (the skill of the action, else of its objective), training-plan items and courses mapped to a skill that no plan action ordered. When the manager validated the action with an observed level that became official, that evidence decides at once; otherwise a validated level within 180 days counts.
k13_den: People with a completed action targeting a skill that had a measured level before.
k13_incl: A first measurement is never an uplift, a self-rating is never a validation, and a level above the requirement is credited at the requirement. People whose 180 days are still running are counted apart.
k14_def: Median number of days from taking up a role to the first « Ready » status.
k14_formula: Kaplan–Meier median of (date of the first « Ready » − role start date): people with a start date who are not ready yet are counted as « still on the way » up to today, never left out (leaving them out would make the median look shorter than it is).
k14_den: People with a recorded role start date and a role with requirements; at least 5 of them reached « Ready ». While fewer than half have reached it, the median is « beyond N days » and not measured.
k14_incl: No start date is ever assumed.
k15_def: Number of validated level increases over the last 90 days.
k15_formula: Number of (person, skill) pairs whose last validated level of the period is above the level held when the period opened.
k15_incl: A first measurement is never a level increase, and a self-assessment is not a validation. No assessment in the period: « Not measured yet ».
k16_def: Counts of the active development plans and, when the development module is on, of the performance improvement plans and coaching plans.
k16_formula: Plans neither draft nor finished (completed, closed, cancelled, withdrawn, rejected, archived); of which « Overdue » = due date passed.
k16_incl: Performance improvement plans are counted only for the people allowed to see them.
alert_k1_coverage_low: Too few requirements are assessed for {{scope}}: {{kpi}} is not reliable while assessment coverage stays below 50 %.
alert_k6_rising: More critical roles have no ready successor than the target allows for {{scope}}.
alert_k9_watch: Some people are no longer cleared for safety for {{scope}}.
alert_k11_late: A running campaign is behind its schedule for {{scope}}.
alert_cta: The dashboard gives the figures and the list behind them.
targets_subtitle: One target per indicator, for the organisation or a site, from a date. Every decision is kept: a change or a withdrawal adds a line to the history.
targets_alerts_note: Alerts fire once when an indicator enters an alert band, again if it gets worse, and a last time when it is back to normal. They name nobody.
targets_field_value_help: A percentage from 0 to 100 (one decimal) or a whole number. Leave it empty to withdraw the target.
targets_audit_note: The decision is written to the audit log with its author, date and reason.
targets_readonly: You are viewing the targets. Setting them needs the « Manage indicator targets » permission on a site, or a SuperAdmin account.
targets_history_empty: No target has been set yet.
targets_unchanged: This decision was already recorded: nothing was added.
targets_err_invalid_scope: Choose the organisation or a site.
targets_err_forbidden: You cannot set a target for this scope.
targets_err_invalid_value: The target must be a percentage from 0 to 100 or a positive whole number.
targets_err_reason_required: Give the reason for the decision.
targets_err_not_found: This indicator is not available: its module is switched off.
k28_def: Did a completed course on a skill move the person's validated level?
k28_formula: Completions of a course mapped to a skill, with a validated level above the level before, ÷ completions with a validated level both before and after (last 12 months).
k28_den: Completions with a validated level before and after, for people of the scope.
k28_incl: A self-rating is never an effect, and a level above the requirement is credited at the requirement. Counted apart, never as 0: no level before, no level after 90 days, a level after still awaited, a course mapped to no skill. Without a course catalogue or a learning platform: « To be set up ».
k28_apart: apart: {{a}} without a level before, {{b}} awaiting a level after, {{c}} not mapped to a skill
k30_def: Do development and coaching plans reach their objectives, in how long, and with how much effort?
k30_formula: Plans achieved (a development plan completed with every objective closed, a coaching validated) ÷ plans achieved or not (completed with open objectives, an active plan stopped), closed in the last 12 months.
k30_den: Development and coaching plans closed in the last 12 months, for people of the scope; cancelled plans apart.
k30_incl: A cancelled plan is never a failure, and filing a completed plan is not a second outcome. Hours are never inferred: an action without hours is « not entered », never 0. Levels per 100 hours only from 5 people who entered their hours. Improvement plans are not counted here.
k30_ageing_line: Active plans past due: {{a}} by up to 30 days, {{b}} by 31 to 90 days, {{c}} by more than 90 days.
k40_def: How many waivers of the safety gate run today, and how the contests of a block are handled.
k40_formula: Waivers active and not yet expired, for people of the scope. Beside it: renewals, the age of the oldest waiver, waivers granted in 30 days by route, open contests and the contests decided in 90 days.
k40_den: People of the scope on a role under an enforced safety rule.
k40_incl: A count, never a list of people. No enforced rule and no waiver ever granted: « To be set up ».
k40_bands: Compliant = no waiver running · Watch while one runs. A waiver is a known shortfall: never compliant while one runs.
k41_def: How many people the safety gate blocks each week, and why.
k41_formula: Entries into an enforced « blocked » status (not the re-evaluations of a person already blocked), per Monday-based week, over 13 weeks; the blocking causes counted per entry.
k41_den: People of the scope on a role under an enforced safety rule.
k41_incl: A week without a nightly recompute and without any entry is « Not measured », never 0. Observe-only and waived causes are not counted. No gate history: « Not measured yet ».
k42_def: How many required certificates expire each month over the next 12 months, by site, if nothing is renewed.
k42_formula: The latest certificate on record of each required (person, skill) pair, by the month of its expiry date, from today to the end of the twelfth month.
k42_den: Required certificates on record for people of the scope (the same rule as K8).
k42_incl: A certificate without an expiry date is counted apart. A site of fewer than 5 people is not named: its certificates are in one « fewer than 5 people » row. Nothing required: « To be set up ».
k43_def: How many minimum-headcount rules of qualified people are in breach now, and how many would break within 30, 60 and 90 days.
k43_formula: Active rules in breach now ÷ active rules you can see. The projection counts, day by day, the qualified people not on planned leave and still holding a certificate not expired that day; it assumes nothing is renewed.
k43_den: Active coverage rules whose whole unit you govern; company-wide rules for SuperAdmins only.
k43_incl: No visible rule: « To be set up ». The projection is an estimate, never a breach.
k43_bands: Compliant = no rule in breach · Watch = a warning rule in breach · At risk = a critical rule in breach.
k44_def: Share of the required certificates on record that carry everything an audit asks for.
k44_formula: Complete records ÷ required certificates on record. Complete = an expiry date (or a policy without expiry), evidence scanned clean, a field sign-off (VOC) and a certificate number. The issuing body is measured as its own rate.
k44_den: Required certificates on record for people of the scope (the same rule as K8).
k44_incl: A required certificate never recorded is counted apart, outside the share. Fewer than 5 people: counts only. Records made before the issuing body could be entered stay « not recorded »; they are never filled in afterwards. The share is rounded down.
k44_bands: Compliant = every record complete · Watch as soon as one is not. Never 100 % while one record is short.
k17_def: How long a submitted self-assessment waits for its decision, and how many people are waiting now.
k17_formula: Median days from submission to approval of the self-assessment rounds submitted in the last 90 days (30 or 365 on request). A round still waiting counts with its age so far (Kaplan–Meier median): the slow cases are never dropped. The 90th percentile is shown from 10 approvals.
k17_den: Rounds of the people of the scope submitted in the window, neither cancelled nor replaced. The backlog: people with a self-assessment waiting for validation now, whatever its age.
k17_incl: A round never submitted is not counted (never « 0 days »). Fewer than 5 approvals: the counts only. When fewer than half were decided, the median is « beyond » the longest wait. No reviewer is ever named.
k17_bands: For information; « Watch » while someone waits more than 7 days. Can carry a target (lower is better, in days).
k19_def: What the people who left took away: were they ready for their role, and were they the only holder of a critical skill of their site?
k19_formula: Leavers of the last 12 months (or 90 days), departure processed and not reverted: how many were ready for their role, and how many held a critical skill nobody else of their site held, as captured on the day they left.
k19_den: Leavers inside your clearance, by the site and department they had when they left.
k19_incl: Read from what was captured at the departure, never reconstructed from today’s requirements. Leavers processed before the capture existed are counted apart as « not measured ». Before the first capture: « Insufficient history ». Counts only.
k20_def: How many people do not meet a legally mandatory safety requirement of their role today.
k20_formula: People of the scope with at least one blocking reason on a legally mandatory safety rule: failed, lapsed, missing, too old, or not shown. Beside it: the waivers in force, the people they cover and the age of the oldest.
k20_den: People of the scope whose role (and site, when the rule is tied to one) carries an active, legally mandatory safety rule.
k20_incl: A legal requirement without evidence is an exposure. A legally mandatory rule cannot be waived. No such rule: « To be set up », never 0. A site under 5 people is counted with the other small sites.
k20_bands: Compliant = nobody exposed · At risk from one person. Never compliant while anyone is exposed.
k21_def: How many critical roles without a ready successor have a holder at high risk of leaving.
k21_formula: Critical roles without a ready successor (the K6 rule) one of whose holders in the scope has a high flight risk.
k21_den: Critical roles with at least one holder in the scope.
k21_incl: A flight risk never reviewed is « not assessed », never « low », and is counted apart. No critical role: « To be set up ». Every uncovered role not assessed: « Not measured ». Counts by role family, never a name. Needs the retention-risk clearance.
k21_bands: Compliant = 0 · Watch = 1 or 2 · At risk = 3 or more. A 0 while roles are not assessed carries no status.
